data.narrative:
Mach Industries is a Series B-stage defense and security company that has raised $185M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 10 comparable companies: 8 private firms at the same stage and sector, plus 2 public defense contractors (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). The private peer set spans valuations from $300M to $3.0B, with a median of $1.1B.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $185M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $352M. Peer-median analysis directly benchmarks Mach against same-sector, same-stage comparables including Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B), producing an implied valuation of $1.1B. The wide dispersion in peer valuations—a 10x spread from floor to ceiling—reflects differentiation in underlying assets, customer concentration, and technology maturity within the defense tech segment.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $299M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $738M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects tension between capital-deployment-based valuation and market-comparable approaches. Key uncertainties include customer concentration risk, differentiation relative to the most highly valued peers, and regulatory headwinds specific to defense-sector exits.
